curation.lead:
America PAC (FEC C00879510) is a Super PAC organized in Texas on May 22, 2024 that served as the primary vehicle for Elon Musk's 2024 presidential election spending. Per FEC financial summaries, the committee raised $263.5 million and disbursed $261.3 million in the 2024 cycle, with 99.25 percent of receipts attributable to individual contributions — effectively all from Musk [Finding #4421]. Independent expenditures totaled $173.7 million, supporting Donald Trump ($173.3 million) and opposing Kamala Harris ($400,000) [Finding #5601].

FEC Schedule B filings and TX Comptroller records show the PAC's operational spending flowed through four Musk-controlled Texas LLCs — Europa 100 LLC, United States of America Inc, Group America LLC, and Excession LLC — which collectively provided approximately $80 million in services [Finding #4384, Finding #4431]. Jared Birchall, Musk's wealth manager, is listed as Secretary of United States of America Inc and Manager of Excession LLC, while Chris Young served as PAC Director and Treasurer, drawing compensation of up to $1 million annually through Europa 100 LLC [Finding #4384].

In the 2025–2026 cycle, FEC records show the PAC had already received $48.2 million in receipts and disbursed $50.2 million through December 2025, with operating expenditures of $37.4 million but only $87,000 in independent expenditures [Finding #4421]. According to a review of court records, the committee faced legal challenges in Pennsylvania, Georgia, North Carolina, Michigan, and three federal courts over its voter payment programs and voter registration activities [Finding #4433].
curation.system_role: America PAC is a federally registered Super PAC (Independent Expenditure-Only Committee) that served as Elon Musk's primary political spending vehicle in the 2024 election cycle, disbursing over $261 million almost entirely funded by Musk's personal contributions and routed through a network of Musk-controlled Texas LLCs.

sections.title: Formation and Structure
sections.content:
America PAC was incorporated in Texas on May 22, 2024, with Chris Young — a Texas-based Republican campaign finance lawyer who operates under the name Chris Gober — listed as founding treasurer [Finding #4421]. The PAC registered with the FEC as an Independent Expenditure-Only Committee (Super PAC) under the identifier C00879510 [Finding #4421]. In July 2024, Phil Cox, a co-founder of political consulting firm GP3 LLC, joined along with colleagues Peck and Rexrode in guiding roles at the PAC [Connection #2636].

Per TX Comptroller records, the PAC's operational spending flowed through four Musk-controlled Texas LLCs. United States of America Inc (TID 32097038932) and Group America LLC (TID 32097028388) were both formed on October 2, 2024, at the same registered address (2025 Guadalupe St Suite 260, Austin TX), with Musk listed as President of USA Inc and Jared Birchall as Secretary. USA Inc is the sole member of Group America LLC. Europa 100 LLC (TID 32075024482) and Excession LLC (TID 32075024201) are older Birchall-managed entities formed July 14, 2020, both using PO Box 341886 Austin TX and Registered Agent Solutions Inc [Finding #4431].

FEC Schedule A receipts show a bidirectional financial relationship: United States of America Inc contributed $47.9 million to America PAC across 12 contributions between November 2024 and June 2025, while America PAC simultaneously made $78.3 million in in-kind contributions back to USA Inc. Additional FEC-documented donors from the Musk entity network include Europa 100 LLC ($3,811), Group America LLC ($3,752 across 4 contributions), Excession LLC ($2,324), 333 Main LLC ($2,840), and the Elon Musk Revocable Trust ($3,425) [Finding #5607, Connection #3028].

sections.title: Financial Activity
sections.content:
Per FEC financial summary data, America PAC raised $263.5 million and disbursed $261.3 million in the 2024 cycle. Elon Musk's direct personal contributions totaled $239.8 million [Finding #5601]. Combined with the $23.7 million channeled via the Musk-controlled LLC network, Musk's total 2024 election spending through this vehicle was estimated by CNN at over $290 million [Finding #4421]. Independent expenditures reached $173.7 million, constituting 66.5 percent of total disbursements [Finding #5601].

The largest single vendor in the 2024 cycle was Blitz Canvassing LLC, which received $54 million or more for canvassing operations [Finding #4467]. Blitz Canvassing is a subsidiary of GP3 LLC, the firm co-founded by Phil Cox, who simultaneously held a guiding position at the PAC [Connection #2636]. FEC Schedule B filings show Cox's firm received $64.6 million from the PAC — approximately 25 percent of total spending — while Cox occupied an operational role directing the same expenditures [Connection #2639, Connection #2636]. According to a review of FEC records and reporting, the PAC replaced an earlier canvassing vendor, September Group (paid $1.4 million), with Blitz Canvassing in September 2024 [Finding #4467].

Additional 2024 cycle vendor payments included Synapse Group LLC ($6 million or more for canvassing) and payments of $1 million each to more than ten spokesperson consultants including Diestler, Jacobs, and Ainsworth [Finding #4467]. In the 2025–2026 cycle, the PAC's largest vendor was USA Inc ($27.3 million in-kind), followed by Lex Politica PLLC ($217,000 legal), IMGE LLC ($92,000 digital), and Rightside Compliance ($30,000) [Finding #4430].

Antonio Gracias, CEO of Valor Equity Partners and a longtime Musk associate, donated $1 million to America PAC in June 2024 [Connection #3029]. FEC records show a shift in Gracias's political giving from primarily Democratic contributions pre-2023 to over $4.1 million in Republican-aligned contributions by January 2025.

sections.title: Key Relationships
sections.content:
Elon Musk is the PAC's sole substantial donor, contributing $239.8 million personally in the 2024 cycle [Finding #5601, Connection #3027]. Combined with entity-level contributions, this total exceeded other major defense-tech political donors such as Peter Thiel ($26.9 million) and Alex Karp ($4.1 million) [Finding #5601]. Musk is listed as President of United States of America Inc, the primary operational entity through which PAC spending flowed [Finding #4431].

Chris Young served simultaneously as Director and Treasurer of America PAC, VP of United States of America Inc, and a DOGE Senior Government Employee deployed to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau — an agency with regulatory authority over Tesla auto loans and X/Visa payment systems. FEC filings indicate Young drew compensation of up to $1 million annually from Europa 100 LLC, a Musk personal entity [Finding #4384, Connection #2637].

Jared Birchall, Musk's wealth manager, holds the Secretary position at United States of America Inc and the Manager position at both Europa 100 LLC and Excession LLC — the entities through which approximately $80 million in services flowed to the PAC [Finding #4431]. FEC records show no personal political contributions from Birchall despite his role managing the operational entities behind a quarter-billion-dollar political spending vehicle.

Phil Cox, co-founder of GP3 LLC, occupied a guiding role at America PAC from July 2024 onward while his firm's subsidiary Blitz Canvassing LLC received $64.6 million — 25 percent of total PAC disbursements [Connection #2639, Connection #2636].

sections.title: Legal Proceedings and Regulatory Actions
sections.content:
America PAC's voter payment programs generated legal challenges across multiple jurisdictions. The PAC offered $47 payments to registered voters in swing states who signed a petition supporting First and Second Amendment rights, later increasing to $100, and ran $1 million daily lottery-style giveaways [Finding #4404]. Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner filed suit in Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court alleging the program constituted an illegal unregulated lottery under Pennsylvania law. Judge Angelo Foglietta declined to enjoin the program in November 2024 after PAC representative Chris Young testified that winners were pre-selected rather than randomly selected — the PAC's legal defense characterizing winners as paid spokespeople rather than lottery participants [Finding #4404].

According to a review of records from multiple jurisdictions, the Georgia State Election Board formally reprimanded the PAC for sending pre-filled absentee ballot applications to voters in Chattooga, Cherokee, Coweta, Floyd, and Whitfield counties, finding the materials violated O.C.G.A. 21-2-381 [Finding #4433]. Records indicate that state-level investigations into voter registration practices were separately initiated in North Carolina and Michigan [Finding #4433].

According to court records, three federal civil cases were filed in 2025: Doe v. America PAC (E.D. Pa. 2:25-cv-01691), Henderson v. America PAC (E.D.N.C. 4:25-cv-00012), and Crawford v. America PAC (D. Ariz. 2:25-cv-00338). Review of court records indicates that the PAC also sought to remove Krasner's Commonwealth Court suit to federal court [Finding #4404, Finding #4433].

The PAC's 2025-2026 cycle shows $37.4 million in operating expenditures but only $87,000 in independent expenditures: what operational activity accounts for the gap during a non-federal-election period?

Chris Young simultaneously served as America PAC Treasurer, USA Inc VP, and DOGE SGE at the CFPB: were any conflict-of-interest disclosures filed with OGE, and do CFPB enforcement or examination records show any action affecting Tesla Auto or X Financial during his tenure?

Blitz Canvassing LLC received $64.6 million from America PAC in 2024 while GP3 co-founder Phil Cox held an operational role at the same PAC: are there FEC or DOJ legal-compliance filings addressing this concurrent vendor-operator arrangement?

FEC records show a circular flow between United States of America Inc and America PAC (USA Inc donates to PAC, PAC makes in-kind contributions to USA Inc): do FEC audit records or IRS filings for USA Inc clarify the economic purpose of this structure and whether any value-at-cost election law requirements were satisfied?
